target.title: fix(auto-reply): treat U+2028/U+2029 as paragraph boundaries when chunking
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chunkByParagraph` normalizes only CR/CRLF before blank-line paragraph detection. When model output uses Unicode LINE SEPARATOR (U+2028) or PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (U+2029) instead of a blank line, those boundaries are not recognized, so paragraph-aware chunking of outbound messages falls back to length-based splitting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize U+2028/U+2029 to `\n` alongside CR/CRLF at the paragraph-detection boundary in `chunkByParagraph`, matching how the Control UI markdown renderer already handles these separators. The regex references the separators via `\u2028` / `\u2029` escapes, so no literal separator character lands in source.

## User Impact

Outbound messages whose paragraphs are delimited by U+2028/U+2029 now split on those paragraph boundaries like blank lines, instead of mid-content length splits. LF/CRLF/CR input is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed:** `chunkByParagraph("paragraph one line\u2028\u2029paragraph two starts here", 40)`

```
AFTER (fixed):  ["paragraph one line","paragraph two starts here"]   (2 chunks)
BEFORE (old):   paragraph boundary NOT detected -> falls to length-based split
```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts` — 67/67 passed (includes the new U+2028/U+2029 regression).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0.
- `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

## Scope

This fixes the paragraph-detection boundary in `chunkByParagraph`. Siblings `splitByNewline` and the top-level `chunkText`/`chunkMarkdownText` breakpoint scanners still key on `\n` only; they are not addressed here to keep this change focused and low-risk.

AI-assisted.
